title: Typing Components
description: Learn how to type React functional components.

data.text: In TypeScript, React components are functions that return JSX. We can type them using `React.FC` or by typing the props directly.

data.title: React.FC
Function Component

data.text: React components return `JSX.Element` or `React.ReactNode`. TypeScript infers this automatically.

cards.title: React.FC<Props>
cards.description: Uses the built-in Functional Component type with generics.

cards.title: Function(props: Props)
cards.description: Types the component as a regular function with props parameter.

cards.title: const Component = (props: Props)
cards.description: Arrow function approach with typed props.
cons: Can be harder to read with complex props

data.title: Recommendation
data.text: The function approach is preferred over React.FC. It's simpler, doesn't include implicit children, and is more explicit.

items.hint: Name it clearly, e.g., ButtonProps or UserCardProps

items.text: Type props in the function parameter
Consider using React.FC for library code
Let TypeScript infer the return type

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Components are functions that return JSX
data.takeaway: Typing components is straightforward with TypeScript.
